title: Compare and Contrast Various Types of Security Controls

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Security controls are safeguards used to reduce risk. CompTIA wants you to recognize them in two different ways:
Category = what kind of control it is and how it is implemented.
Type = what the control is trying to accomplish.
That distinction is the heart of Objective 1.1.

sections.title: Category vs. Type
paragraphs: A single security control can have both a category and a type because those labels answer different questions.
For example, a firewall is a Technical control because technology implements it. It can also be a Preventive control because its purpose is to stop unauthorized traffic.
sections.callout: First ask HOW the control is implemented. Then ask WHY the control exists.

sections.title: Security Control Categories
paragraphs: A category describes what kind of control you are looking at and how it is carried out.

entries.title: Technical
paragraphs: A technical control uses hardware, software, or another technology to enforce security.
Think: “The computer or system is doing the protecting.”

entries.title: Managerial
paragraphs: A managerial control deals with governance and decision-making.
Think: “Management decided what security should look like.”

entries.title: Operational
paragraphs: An operational control depends primarily on people and processes.
Think: “A person or team carries this out.”

entries.title: Physical
paragraphs: A physical control protects facilities, equipment, people, or physical access.
examples: A badge reader controls building access
A security guard watches and controls entry
entries.recognitionCue: If it protects or controls something you can physically touch → Physical

table.caption: Security control category recognition sheet
rows: Leadership, planning, policy, and risk-management controls
People and day-to-day procedures carry out the control
Protects physical locations, equipment, or people

sections.title: Security Control Types
paragraphs: Now CompTIA changes the question. Instead of asking what category it is, the exam may ask: “What is the control trying to accomplish?”
A type describes the main purpose of the control.

entries.title: Preventive
paragraphs: Preventive controls try to stop the incident before it succeeds.
examples: Blocking unauthorized access before an attacker succeeds

entries.title: Deterrent
paragraphs: A deterrent control tries to make someone decide, “I probably should not try that.” It may not physically stop the person, but it discourages the behavior.

entries.title: Detective
paragraphs: A detective control identifies activity that has happened or is happening.

entries.title: Corrective
paragraphs: A corrective control helps repair damage or restore the environment after a problem occurs.

entries.title: Compensating
paragraphs: A compensating control is an alternative safeguard used when the preferred control is not practical or possible.
examples: The preferred security measure cannot be deployed on a legacy system, so another control is placed around it to reduce risk
entries.recognitionCue: Cannot use the normal control, so use another one → Compensating

entries.title: Directive
paragraphs: A directive control tells users what they must or should do. Policies, instructions, and required procedures can serve this purpose.

table.caption: Security control type recognition sheet
rows: Fix or recover after something happened
Use an alternative when the preferred control cannot be used
Tell people what they are expected to do

sections.title: Recognition Cues
paragraphs: When you read a Security+ scenario, first identify whether the question is asking about category or type.
bullets: Policy, governance, or risk decision → Managerial
Facility, equipment, or physical access → Physical
Alternative because the preferred control cannot be used → Compensating
Tells people what they must do → Directive
sections.callout: Category asks HOW. Type asks WHY.

sections.title: ⚠️ Objective 1.1 Exam Trap
paragraphs: A control can belong to a category and a type at the same time.
A security camera can be in the Physical category and have a Detective type.
A firewall can be in the Technical category and have a Preventive type.
Those classifications are answering different questions, so they are not competing answers.
sections.callout: Do not force category and type to compete. Classify the same control once by HOW and once by WHY.

miniCheck.intro: Use the two-question method: first identify HOW the control is implemented, then identify WHY it is being used.
miniCheck.prompt: A company installs a security camera to identify unauthorized entry after hours.
miniCheck.correctFeedback: Correct. The camera is Physical because it is a physical security device. Its purpose is Detective because it identifies and records unauthorized activity.
miniCheck.retryFeedback: Not quite. Ask two separate questions: HOW is the control implemented, and WHY was it installed? Review the recognition cues and try again.
